messages.text: HMRC asked to explore tax implications of Man City case

metadata.summary: The Treasury Committee has written to the chief executive of HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) to ask about the tax implications of the Premier League's investigation into Manchester City.
metadata.content: Man City charges: Treasury Committee writes to HMRC to ask about tax implications of Premier League investigation | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City charges: Treasury Committee writes to HMRC to ask about tax implications of Premier League investigation Man City have been found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City deny all charges and have confirmed they will appeal against the ruling and have until Friday to do so Thursday 1 October 2026 20:01, UK Image: An aerial view over the Etihad Stadium in Manchester The Treasury Committee has written to the chief executive of HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) to ask about the tax implications of the Premier League's investigation into Manchester City. HMRC could investigate whether City paid the right amount of tax and national insurance during the nine seasons they have been found guilty of financial rule breaches. In the letter, Dame Meg Hillier MP asks JP Marks, permanent secretary of HMRC, whether the department has received an unredacted version of the Premier League's report and requests "reassurance from HMRC that you are seized of the importance of these issues and the public interest in the case". metadata.summary: World No 979 Michael Stewart outscored a big-name field to share the lead at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship after a first-round 65.
metadata.content: Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: World No 979 Michael Stewart claims share of lead with Matt Fitzpatrick, Tommy Fleetwood further back | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Alfred Dunhill Links Championship: World No 979 Michael Stewart claims share of lead with Matt Fitzpatrick, Tommy Fleetwood further back The Alfred Dunhill Links Championship is played over three courses – Carnoustie, Kingsbarns and St Andrews with the Old Course hosting the final day – and also incorporates a team event with a number of former sports stars and celebrities paired with the professionals Thursday 1 October 2026 18:39, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day one of the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship World No 979 Michael Stewart outscored a big-name field to share the lead at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship after a first-round 65. The 36-year-old has played only five DP World Tour events - the last in 2023 - and teed off less than 24 hours after finishing second in the Tartan Tour's Duddingston Classic having received a sponsor's invite earlier this week. He had a remarkable back nine at Carnoustie, where an eagle at the par-five 12th was the catalyst to play five holes in six under par. metadata.summary: England have avoided fellow heavyweights Australia and India in the group stage of the 2027 Men's 50-over World Cup in Africa.
metadata.content: 2027 Cricket World Cup: England avoid Australia and India in group stage as fixtures revealed for 50-over tournament | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content 2027 Cricket World Cup: England avoid Australia and India in group stage as fixtures revealed for 50-over tournament England drawn alongside South Africa, New Zealand, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and qualifier for pool phase of event that runs from October 2 to November 21, 2027; World Cup final will be held at Wanderers in Johannesburg, the same venue for the India vs Pakistan match on October 10 Thursday 1 October 2026 18:38, UK Image: England have been grouped with South Africa, New Zealand, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and a qualifier for the 2027 Cricket World Cup England have avoided fellow heavyweights Australia and India in the group stage of the 2027 Men's 50-over World Cup in Africa. Harry Brook's side are placed in Group B alongside New Zealand, co-hosts South Africa, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and a qualifier for a tournament that runs from October 2 to November 21 next year. Defending champions Australia join India, Pakistan, Afghanistan, another co-host Zimbabwe and a qualifier in Group A of the event. messages.text: How Man City plan to argue their innocence in appeal

metadata.summary: Manchester City will argue in their Premier League appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals between 2009 and 2018 came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's owners.
metadata.content: Man City charges: How Premier League club plan to argue their innocence in appeal | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Man City charges: How Premier League club plan to argue their innocence in appeal Man City plan to appeal before Friday's deadline after an independent commission found they broke Premier League financial rules by disguising £830m of owner funding as sponsorship income Lyall Thomas Senior Football News Editor @SkySportsLyall Thursday 1 October 2026 20:12, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol breaks down Manchester City's strategy to appeal the verdict Manchester City will argue in their Premier League appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals between 2009 and 2018 came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's owners. An independent commission has found that City broke Premier League financial rules by disguising £830.69m of owner funding as sponsorship income. City's lawyers argued during the 2024 hearing that the funding had come from the Abu Dhabi government, but this was rejected by the commission.
